# CI & release — the macOS DMG

How `LaughCounter.dmg` reaches users, and the workflow-trigger gotchas learned
wiring it up. Read before editing `.github/workflows/release-macos-dmg.yml` or
`build-macos-dmg.yml`.

**The shape.** `release-macos-dmg.yml` owns `main`: on a push to `main` touching
`mac/**` it builds the DMG, derives `v<version>` from `mac/Resources/Info.plist`,
and creates/updates that GitHub Release with `LaughCounter.dmg` attached — so the
README's stable `releases/latest/download/LaughCounter.dmg` link always resolves.
`build-macos-dmg.yml` is the feature-branch artifact builder and **excludes
`main`** (`branches: ["**", "!main"]`) so it never duplicates the release build.

## Trigger the release on push-to-main, not a `v*` tag push

A Claude Code **web session pushes through a git-only proxy that cannot push
`v*` tags**, so a release workflow keyed on `push: tags` never fires from a
session — the Release area stays empty and the `latest/download` link 404s. Key
the release on **push to `main`** (scoped to `mac/**`) instead: the job derives
`v<version>` from `Info.plist` and creates the tag + Release with `GITHUB_TOKEN`,
which *can* tag and release from within Actions even though the session can't.
(#18 / #19)

## A UI-published Release does not fire `push: tags` — add `release: published`

Publishing a Release from the GitHub UI creates the tag but does **not** emit a
`push: tags` event, so a workflow listening only for tag pushes won't build for
it. Keep a `release: types: [published]` trigger alongside the push-to-main one so
a hand-published Release still builds and attaches the DMG. (#11 / #13)

## Why the two triggers don't loop or double-build

- The tag + Release the push-to-main job creates is made with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and
  a Release created by `GITHUB_TOKEN` does **not** re-fire the `release` event —
  so the `release: published` trigger doesn't re-run it. (This is the canon's
  general "`GITHUB_TOKEN` doesn't start another workflow" rule, applied to the
  `release` event specifically.)
- `build-macos-dmg.yml` excludes `main`, so a `mac/**` push to `main` builds once
  (in the release job), not twice.

## Signing & notarization is an optional, secret-gated lane (#4)

Both DMG workflows have an **optional** Developer ID signing + Apple notarization
lane that runs only when the signing secrets are set (`MACOS_CERT_P12`,
`MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD`, `MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`,
`APPLE_APP_PASSWORD`); without them the build still passes and ships an **ad-hoc**
DMG. **Keep it secret-gated** — never make signing a required step, or a fork or
secret-less build breaks. The signing/notarization how-to and the user-facing
Gatekeeper steps live in `mac/README.md`; `scripts/build-app.sh` signs and
`scripts/notarize-dmg.sh` notarizes + staples. The CI-side gotchas that aren't in
the README:

- **Notarization requires the Hardened Runtime** (`codesign --options runtime`),
  and under it the mic needs an explicit entitlement
  (`com.apple.security.device.audio-input`, in
  `mac/Resources/LaughCounter.entitlements`) that an ad-hoc build doesn't — so
  turning on notarization silently kills mic access unless the entitlement ships
  with it. (Speech recognition is gated by TCC + the Info.plist usage string, not
  a codesign entitlement, so it needs nothing there.)
- **An ad-hoc signature can't be notarized** — they're separate lanes; only the
  Developer-ID-signed `.app` (built when `MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY` is set) can be
  submitted to the notary service.
- **The ephemeral signing keychain must be added to the searchable keychain
  list** (`security list-keychains -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN" $(security
  list-keychains -d user | sed …)`) or `codesign` can't find the imported
  identity. That `sed` pipe is why the workflows set `defaults.run.shell: bash`
  for pipefail (#27; enforced by the canon `gha/run-pipefail` check).
- **macOS 15 (Sequoia) removed the right-click → Open Gatekeeper bypass** — the
  ad-hoc install path is now System Settings → Privacy & Security → *Open Anyway*,
  or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <app>` (see `mac/README.md`).
- This is the **non–App Store** track (no App Sandbox); a Mac App Store build
  would need the App Sandbox and a different Apple Distribution certificate.

**PR [#100](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/100) squashed to `main` as `b6bfe51`, closing #88. Shipping as v0.5.0 (build 10).**

| Step | Result |
|---|---|

| CI on head commit `d67547a` | green — app built, DMG packaged |
| Squash merge to `main` | done |
| Local `main` synced | done |
| Conversation capture (`--issue 88`) | 356 entries → `conversation-logs` |
| Release workflow → `v0.5.0` + DMG | running, I'll confirm when it lands |

Minor bump rather than patch because this changes *behaviour* around the input device, not just what the app reports — it no longer opens the microphone to find out whether one exists.

The build number moved too. Per #74's lesson, the release keys the Release on `CFBundleShortVersionString` alone, so `CFBundleVersion` is the only thing separating two builds shipped under one version — which previously meant reading symbol names out of a crash report to tell them apart.

Once the release job finishes, the [latest-download link](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/releases/latest/download/LaughCounter.dmg) will serve 0.5.0. It's an ad-hoc build (no signing secrets set), so installing is System Settings → Privacy & Security → *Open Anyway*, or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`.

> ⚠️ One thing genuinely open, and worth remembering when you next see this: **0.5.0 is not a proven fix for the mic dying.** It removes ~210 device-open/aggregate-churn cycles per outage — the one abnormal thing we did — and it stops the menu bar lying about it. Whether that churn was the actual cause is unproven; the BRIO reported a sane `48000Hz/2ch/alive=y` at the moment we grabbed it, which argues against the mid-enumeration story specifically. If it recurs on 0.5.0, that's a real data point rather than a failed gate, and `dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md` says so, so the next session won't mistake this for settled. You'll now find out within ~60 seconds via ⚠️ instead of hours later.

Comment class: correction — a regression I introduced in 0.5.0.

You're right, and I can see the cause. It's the settle gate I added.

At launch `AudioDiagnostics.start()` schedules its sampler with `Timer(timeInterval: 5, repeats: true)` — which **first fires 5 seconds later**. `usableInputSince` is only ever set inside `sample()`, so for the first 5s `usableInputFor` is `nil` and my gate refuses. Then the clock starts from zero and needs another 6s. The retry ladder backs off 2s → 4s → 8s, so the first attempt that can succeed lands around **t≈19s**.

So it does start eventually — but ~19 seconds of silence at every launch reads exactly as "it didn't start," and you shouldn't have to wait or click.

The deeper error is conceptual: **the settle gate should only apply to an arrival we actually witnessed.** A device already present when our process starts has been there for however long the Mac has been up — there is no enumeration race to lose. "It appeared N seconds ago" is a claim I can only make about a transition I saw.

input.head: claude/sound-input-sleep-issue-9eh40k
input.body:
Fixes a regression shipped in 0.5.0 (#100), reported on install: the counter does not start listening at launch and has to be switched on by hand.

## Cause

The settle gate added in #100 refused to open the microphone for **~19 seconds** after launch. Two compounding faults:

**1. The sampler's first tick is 5 seconds late.** `Timer(timeInterval:repeats:)` does not fire immediately, and `usableInputSince` was only ever set inside `sample()`. So for the app's first five seconds `usableInputFor` was `nil` and `requireSettledInputDevice()` refused — reporting "no input hardware" about a microphone sitting right there. Any state a timer maintains needs **seeding at start**, not just updating on tick.

**2. The settle clock then started from first observation**, costing another 6s. With the ladder's 2s → 4s → 8s backoff, the first attempt that could succeed landed at ~19s.

## The conceptual error

The second fault is the real one, and it's the reusable lesson:

> *"It appeared N seconds ago" is a claim you can only make about a transition you watched happen.*

A device already present when sampling began has been there for as long as the Mac has been up. There is no enumeration race to lose, and waiting is pure cost. I had applied a settle window to *presence* when it only ever made sense for *arrival*.

## Fix

- `AudioDiagnostics.start()` seeds the probe from the first device look it already takes for `lastDevices`.
- `usableInputFor` returns `.greatestFiniteMagnitude` for a device found already present (`witnessedArrival == false`), and a real duration only for one seen to arrive.

**The wedge case is unaffected.** The mic vanishing and returning — the whole reason the gate exists — is a witnessed arrival and still gets its full 6s settle window before we open it. Launch returns to starting capture ~0.4s in, as in 0.4.1.

## Verification

`swift build` can't run in a Linux session; the branch DMG workflow compiles on macOS. Per `dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md`, compile-green is not a gate for this file — the real check is that the menu bar shows 😄 within a second or two of launch, without touching the menu.

`dev/procedures/mac-audio-lifecycle.md` records both faults under the settle-gate section, since the timer-seeding one is the kind that recurs.

Ships as **0.5.1 (build 11)**.

content.text:
CI green on `2ac228e4`, the head of PR #101 — it compiles and the DMG builds.

## What went wrong

You're right that it's wrong, and it's mine. The settle gate I added in 0.5.0 refused to open the mic for **~19 seconds** after launch. Two faults stacked:

**The sampler's first tick is 5 seconds late.** `Timer(timeInterval:repeats:)` doesn't fire immediately, and I only ever set `usableInputSince` inside `sample()`. So for the app's first five seconds the probe reported "no input hardware" about a microphone sitting right there. State a timer maintains needs seeding at `start()`, not only updating on tick.

**Then the settle clock ran from first observation**, costing another 6s — and with the retry ladder's 2s → 4s → 8s backoff, the first attempt that could succeed landed at ~19s. It does eventually start, but nobody waits 19 seconds staring at a menu bar, and they shouldn't have to.

The second one is the real error, and it's conceptual: *"it appeared N seconds ago" is a claim you can only make about a transition you watched happen.* A device already present when sampling begins has been there as long as the Mac has been up — no enumeration race to lose, so waiting is pure cost. I applied a settle window to **presence** when it only ever made sense for **arrival**.

## The fix — PR [#101](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/101), ships as 0.5.1 (build 11)

- `start()` seeds the probe from the device look it already takes.
- `usableInputFor` returns "settled" for a device found already present, and a real duration only for one seen to arrive.

**The wedge gate is intact.** Your mic vanishing and returning is a witnessed arrival and still gets its full 6s window before we open it. Launch goes back to starting capture ~0.4s in, as in 0.4.1.

Also confirmed: **v0.5.0 published with its DMG**, so the [latest-download link](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/releases/latest/download/LaughCounter.dmg) resolves.

> ⚠️ Open: PR #101 is green and awaiting your LGTM — merging cuts v0.5.1, which is the build worth having on the machine before the next sleep. **Worth knowing for your test:** the 0.5.0 you're running right now *does* still start listening on its own after ~19s, so if you've left it on, tonight's sleep is still a valid test of the churn fix — the launch bug delays startup, it doesn't disable it. And I bumped the version without you asking; say so if you'd rather it had stayed 0.5.0.

0.5.0 refused to start listening for ~19 seconds after launch, which
reads as "it doesn't start" and made the owner switch it on by hand.
The settle gate added in #100 caused it, two ways:

- Timer(timeInterval:repeats:) does not fire immediately, so the first
  sample lands 5s after AudioDiagnostics.start(). usableInputSince was
  only ever set inside sample(), so for the app's first five seconds
  the probe reported "no input device" about a microphone sitting right
  there. start() now seeds the probe from the first look it already
  takes for lastDevices.
- The settle clock then started from first *observation*, costing
  another 6s, and the ladder's 2->4->8s backoff pushed the first viable
  attempt to ~19s.

The second is the real error. "It appeared N seconds ago" is a claim
that can only be made about a transition we watched happen — a device
already present when sampling began has been there for as long as the
Mac has been up, so there is no enumeration race to lose and waiting is
pure cost. A settle window was applied to presence when it only ever
made sense for arrival.

usableInputFor now reports .greatestFiniteMagnitude for a device found
already present (witnessedArrival == false) and a real duration only
for one seen to arrive. The wedge case is unaffected: the mic vanishing
and coming back is a witnessed arrival, and still gets its full 6s
settle window before we open it. Launch returns to starting capture
~0.4s in, as in 0.4.1.

Ships as 0.5.1 (build 11).
